Add a new GetAudioChannelMapping call to the API This is necessary because audio channels may be remapped by the Chameleon FPGA. For instance the first channel of a HDMI/DisplayPort audio signal will be re-mapped to the second channel in the captured pages. BUG=chromium:950922 TEST=Call GetAudioChannelMapping for audio ports that support capture Change-Id: Id3354c65c081f9b581cad402d334d39cfd611237 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1561231 Commit-Ready: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org>

Don't reset HDMI audio receiver if input is stable This commit adds a new IsAudioInputStable method to HdmiRx, similar to the DpRx one. If audio input is stable when ResetAudioLogic is called, there's no need to reset the audio receiver. BUG=chromium:955401 TEST=Use StartCapturingAudio twice without stopping audio playback on the DUT Change-Id: I338f9d8a6da4901c4c1924c3f0f86ca06e779f00 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1578798 Commit-Ready: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org>

Add a new GetAudioFormat call for audio ports This call allows clients to retrieve the capture audio format currently in use, including the sample rate. For DisplayPort the sample rate is read from the receiver. For HDMI it's still hardcoded (I'm not comfortable with implementing it given I can't test it). In my tests the DisplayPort receiver returned an unknown sample rate when sending a 44.1KHz signal. It reports correct sample rates for 32KHz and 48KHz signals. I guess we can't do a lot more than documenting it. BUG=chromium:950913 TEST=Start playing audio on the DUT, call StartCapturingAudio and then call GetAudioFormat. Change-Id: I8b064b2ec0f388f223bc0c32ed06c7e3643bb2a4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1564476 Commit-Ready: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org>

Prevent Reset failures due to StopCapturingAudio If StopCapturingAudio raises an exception, this will interrupt the Reset process and leave the Chamelium device in a bad state. StopCapturingAudio can raise an exception e.g. if no audio data has been captured. Treat StopCapturingAudio errors as non-fatal by logging them. BUG=chromium:955999 TEST=Call StartCapturingAudio without playing audio, then call Reset Change-Id: I9cb98fe9e6fcd439c7ecd0d3d346881cc6365a65 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1583770 Commit-Ready: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: ARM: dts: rockchip: Add all CPUs in cooling maps Each CPU can (and does) participate in cooling down the system but the DT only captures a handful of them, normally CPU0, in the cooling maps. Things work by chance currently as under normal circumstances its the first CPU of each cluster which is used by the operating systems to probe the cooling devices. But as soon as this CPU ordering changes and any other CPU is used to bring up the cooling device, we will start seeing failures. Also the DT is rather incomplete when we list only one CPU in the cooling maps, as the hardware doesn't have any such limitations. Update cooling maps to include all devices affected by individual trip points. Signed-off-by: Viresh Kumar <viresh.kumar@linaro.org> Signed-off-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de> (cherry picked from commit 99935bd4b5b4558beb069222e6d6143fe5830d64) BUG=chromium:941638 TEST=build for minnie Change-Id: Ib3899e5fd46dc1b8f57cfc4e53bea4d87389d695 Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1566079 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Tested-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>
